# dsh-effort-slider

A reasoning-effort slider that **replaces the shipped model selector** in the dsh
web GUI composer.

One control owns both halves of the model choice: the model
list and that model's reasoning effort,

which becomes a glowing rail with a
starfield behind it.
**中文**：把 dsh 输入框里的模型选择器换成一条"星光滑轨"——模型列表与思考强度由同一个控件管，切到不支持当前档位的模型时自动落到最接近的一档，不再报错。
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Screenshots

The rail is drawn from the model's own `reasoning.efforts`, so the tick labels
change with the model

— `off / low / high / max` on one, `low / medium / high /
xhigh / max` on another — and the knob la

nds on the level the session is
actually using.
## What it does

- Takes over `conversation.input.model` (a single slot, so this shadows the
shipped selector rather

than sitting next to it) at `priority: -1` — a single
slot renders the **lowest** priority first.
-

Reads the model catalogue at runtime: the model list comes from
`catalog.groups` (grouped by provide

r) and the levels are exactly the
`reasoning.efforts` the current model declares (typically `off / l

ow / high /
max`). No hard-coded list.
- Shows the Session's **real** selection, not the deployment

default, by reading
the durable `modelSelection` projection.
- Picking a level or a model calls the

session `selectModel` remote with the
explicit `{ provider, model, reasoningEffort }` triple, so the

choice applies to
the Session and is saved as the default in the background.
- Switching to a model

that does not declare the level in hand is resolved on the
client first: the closest level that mod

el *does* declare is sent instead, and
the status line says which substitution happened. A model wit

h no reasoning at
all is switched to with the field omitted, so the Host applies that model's own
de

fault. Nothing errors, nothing is silently dropped.
- The rail is animated: drifting particles, soft

ribbon waves, iridescent
four-point stars, a breathing star core, and a three-armed galaxy that
col

lapses out of the rail at the top level. Reaching the top fires a shockwave
burst, a star-warp starf

ield and a light-blade flash.
- The composer itself carries the light: a halo wraps the whole input

card, with
the same hue as the rail. Brightness, ring alpha and glow radius all follow the
level, so

`off` is a faint rim and the top level breathes; opening the panel
lifts it. The pill only keeps an

outline while the halo is on.
- The halo is a setting, not a hard rule. A `外圈光环` switch sits under

. The choice is stored in `localStorage` under
`effort-slider:halo`, so it survives a reload.
- The

halo knows its place in the page. It is a body-level layer at `z-index: 30`
[该节后续省略]
## Surfaces
| Slot | Content |
| `conversation.input.model` | the trigger (`模型 · 档位`) and, while open, the popup: model row, groupe

d model list, effort rail, level scale, status line |
| `conversation.input.model.label` | untouched
— the shipped non-interactive label stays owner-managed |

The popup renders through `react-dom`'s `createPortal` into `document.body`,
because the composer ro

w can live inside a transformed/overflowing ancestor that
would clip a `position: fixed` child.
## Why a model switch remaps the effort

The Host validates the triple, it does not normalize it. In
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` → `resolveCallWit

t validates the triple, it does not normalize it. In
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` → `resolveCallWithInfo`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The comment above it is explicit: *"no clamping or aliasing is performed."* A
model with three rungs

and a model with seven therefore reject each other's
levels, and the session remote wraps that reje

ction as
`RemoteError("session/model-unavailable", …)` — which used to surface as a red
`切换失败：provid
er "…" model "…" does not support reasoning effort "…"`.

So `resolveEffort(model, wantedId)` in `client.js` maps the level onto the target
model before the r

t(model, wantedId)` in `client.js` maps the level onto the target
model before the request is built:
| Case | What is sent | Status line |

| target declares the level | it, unchanged | nothing |
| target declares other levels | the closest

one | `该模型没有「medium」档，已自动切到最接近的「low」` |
| target declares no reasoning | the field is **omitted** |
`「<model>」没有思考强度档位，已按模型默认运行` |

"Closest" is measured on one shared scale rather than per-provider lists, because
every adapter name

s its rungs from the same vocabulary:
`off · none · minimal · low · medium/med · high · xhigh · max

· ultra`. A tie
resolves to the **stronger** rung — losing reasoning power is the worse of the two
s

urprises (`high → xhigh` rather than `high → medium` when both are one step
away). A rung whose id i

s not on that scale is placed by its position in its own
list, and when the id being carried is itse

lf unknown the target's
`defaultEffort` (then its strongest rung) is used instead, because its dista

nce
cannot be measured.

The last real choice is remembered in `lastEffort`, so
`max → 无档位模型 → back` returns to `max` instead

of that model's default: the
intent survives the models that cannot express it.
## Why every visible label is passed through `safeLabel`

dsh-pocket installs a document-level click guard for phones: any click on a
`<button>`/`<a>` whose *

*text content** looks like a file path is cancelled with
`preventDefault()` + `stopImmediatePropagat

ion()` and replaced by a toast
("手机上无法直接打开电脑上的文件"). Its matcher includes
`/[\w.\-]+\/[\w.\-]+\.\w{1,

12}/`, which a model id like
`workbuddy-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash` matches — so the trigger became uncl

ickable on
mobile while working fine on the desktop.

Every label rendered as text therefore runs through `safeLabel()`, which turns
`/` and `\` into ` ·

`. `aria-label` and `title` keep the raw identifier, because
they are attributes and the guard only
reads `textContent`.
